notes.f1: Agent asserted the forbidden parentage again: R11 links Magdalena (I1) to Catharina Gosnerin. This run actually surfaced the correct hypothesis (h_002: two different wives named Catharina) but ruled it out, reasoning 'no death or remarriage record supports this reading' -- it never found the 1751 marriage record (a different collection) that would have confirmed h_002 instead.
notes.f2: Agent wrote a positive 'probable' conclusion instead of the required negative one, for the same reason as f1. A prior grader on this same text called this 'partial, not unreasoned': five sources rather than one, sibling correlation across 1741-1756, two competing hypotheses stated, a mentor critique recorded, and an honest statement of its own ceiling (all sources derivative, original Triesen Kirchenbuch not examined) -- real, credited analysis, not carelessness. That reasoning stands, but it argues for a high proof_quality_score on a sound process, not for partial recall: f2's own text requires a documented negative conclusion specifically and says 'leaving the question open as unresolved does not satisfy this finding' -- this run didn't leave it open, it asserted the opposite of what was required. Per-finding grades whether that required conclusion got written, not how carefully the wrong one was reasoned; this run's actual proof_quality_score (1, unsound) is where the conclusion being wrong, despite the real work around it, is captured instead.
